note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative; jurisdiction unspecified. 'Admitted' and 'disputed' are only states supplied for this example: nothing states an effect of admitting or disputing, a burden of proof, a consequence or an outcome. The two scenes differ only in the state supplied for the first section. Long-labels-stress: coordinator decision (standing stress rule, AUTHORING item 20, 2026-09-26): the shared-strip texts and the roles are capped (see the preset description); scenario labels, names, case file and day labels keep their near-maximum lengths.

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Near-maximum lengths in the scenario labels, party names, case file and day labels; counts as in LAW-0257's capped stress preset. Coordinator decision (standing stress rule, AUTHORING item 20, 2026-09-26): the texts printed in the shared strip and the roles are capped to the longest values found to keep every ratio at text >= 16 px with people at head >= 45 px (the contrast floor of LAW-0251 / LAW-0447) — scenario captions 'The first section marks the delivery allegation admitted, exactly as supplied here' 82 → 'Delivery marked admitted, as supplied' 37; 'The first section marks the delivery allegation disputed, exactly as supplied here' 82 → 'Delivery marked disputed, as supplied' 37; changed fact 'The state supplied for the first section of the structured response (admitted in A, disputed in B), nothing else' 112 → 'The state supplied for section 1 (A admitted, B disputed)' 57; shared facts 2 → 1 ('Same allegations of the initial claim, same sections · Same fictional parties, case file, trays and calendar' 108 → 'Same allegations, sections, parties, trays and calendar' 55); guide 'Only the first section’s thread and its supplied state differ here' 66 → 'Only the first section’s thread and its supplied state differ' 61; neutral note 'Two configured states shown side by side for illustration; no conclusion, winner or effect is drawn' 99 → 'Shown side by side for illustration; no conclusion is drawn' 59; roles 'Respondent answering the claim (fictional)' 42 → 'Respondent (fictional)' 22; 'Claimant who filed the claim (fictional)' 40 → 'Claimant (fictional)' 20; titles 'Initial claim filed by Party A (fictional)' 42 → 'Initial claim by Party A (fictional)' 36; 'Structured response by Party B (fictional)' 42 → 'Response by Party B (fictional)' 31; allegations 'The borrowed item reached Party B on Day 1' 42 → 'The item reached Party B on Day 1' 33; 'The item came back with a cracked casing' 40 → 'It came back with a cracked casing' 34; 'No repair or replacement was offered' 36 → 'No repair or replacement offered' 32; sections 'Section 1 · on the delivery of the item' 39 → 'Section 1 · on the delivery' 27; 'Section 2 · on the condition on return' 38 → 'Section 2 · on the condition' 28; 'Section 3 · on any offer of repair' 34 → 'Section 3 · on any repair offer' 31. The scenario labels and party names keep their near-maximum lengths. True driver: at 1:1 the shared strip (every supplied text printed once at >= 16 px) and the two scenes share the frame height; the scenes' height sets the people. Measured (rendered, 1:1): with the near-maximum values head 30 px; with the first caps 40–41 px; capped as above 48.1 px (seated Party A; Party B 53.7), with the two changed-thread insets at the head of the strip. Tried first: stacked scenes with the strip in a side column, hanging-board scenes, larger people scales (up to 2.1), captions moved from the headers to the strip, and bar-only scene sheets.
